pthm-nrqm-composites-local-statistics-of.before:
**(b) Non-product pure preparations are correlated.** If $\Psi$ is not a
product vector and
$\Psi=\sum_{r\in J}s_{r}\kappa(v_{r}\otimes u_{r})$ is its Schmidt expansion
with $s_{1}\ge s_{2}>0$, then the rank-one effects
$P:=T_{v_{1},v_{1}}$ on $H$ and $P':=T_{u_{2},u_{2}}$ on $K$ satisfy
$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(P\otimes P')\bigr)=s_{2}^{2}\ \ne\ s_{1}^{2}s_{2}^{2}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}P)\;\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{B}P'),$$
so the joint law of the corresponding two-outcome local measurements does not
factorize; the difference is $s_{2}^{2}(1-s_{1}^{2})>0$.
pthm-nrqm-composites-local-statistics-of.after:
**(b) Non-product pure preparations are correlated.** If $\Psi$ is not a
product vector and
$\Psi=\sum_{r\in J}s_{r}\kappa(v_{r}\otimes u_{r})$ is its Schmidt expansion
with $s_{1}\ge s_{2}>0$, then the rank-one effects
$P:=T_{v_{1},v_{1}}$ on $H$ and $P':=T_{u_{2},u_{2}}$ on $K$ satisfy
$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(P\otimes P')\bigr)=0\ \ne\ s_{1}^{2}s_{2}^{2}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}P)\;\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{B}P'),$$

factorize; the product of the marginal probabilities exceeds the joint

pthm-nrqm-composites-local-statistics-of.before: 1.2 [Non-product case] Let $\Psi$ be non-product with Schmidt expansion $\Psi=\sum_{r}s_{r}\kappa(v_{r}\otimes u_{r})$, $s_{1}\ge s_{2}>0$, and put $P=T_{v_{1},v_{1}}$, $P'=T_{u_{2},u_{2}}$. Since $(P\otimes P')\kappa(v_{r}\otimes u_{r})=\kappa(Pv_{r}\otimes P'u_{r})=\delta_{r,2}\,\kappa(v_{2}\otimes u_{2})$ by [F3] and [F2], one has $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(P\otimes P'))=\langle(P\otimes P')\Psi,\Psi\rangle=s_{2}^{2}$ by [F2]. On the other hand $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}P)=s_{1}^{2}$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{B}P')=s_{2}^{2}$ by [F1] and [F2], so the two sides differ by $s_{2}^{2}(1-s_{1}^{2})$, which is positive because $s_{2}>0$ and $s_{1}^{2}<1$ when two coefficients are nonzero. [given, F1, F2, F3, algebra]
pthm-nrqm-composites-local-statistics-of.after: 1.2 [Non-product case] Let $\Psi$ be non-product. By [F1] its norm-convergent Schmidt expansion has at least two positive coefficients; label two of them $s_{1}\ge s_{2}>0$ and put $P=T_{v_{1},v_{1}}$, $P'=T_{u_{2},u_{2}}$. Since $Pv_{r}=\delta_{r,1}v_{1}$ and $P'u_{r}=\delta_{r,2}u_{2}$ by the rank-one definition and orthonormality, [F3] gives $(P\otimes P')\kappa(v_{r}\otimes u_{r})=\delta_{r,1}\delta_{r,2}\kappa(v_{1}\otimes u_{2})=0$ for every $r$. Boundedness of $P\otimes P'$ passes this identity through the norm-convergent Schmidt expansion, so $(P\otimes P')\Psi=0$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(P\otimes P'))=0$ by [F2]. The trace-norm expansions of the reduced preparations [F1], paired with the bounded projections, give $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}P)=s_{1}^{2}$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{B}P')=s_{2}^{2}$ by [F2]. Thus the marginal product exceeds the joint probability by $s_{1}^{2}s_{2}^{2}>0$. The two local measurements $(P,I-P)$ and $(P',I-P')$ are effect families by [F2], [F4], and their $(+,+)$ entry already proves nonfactorization. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

pthm-nrqm-composites-local-statistics-of.location: Remarks: One pair of effects suffices
pthm-nrqm-composites-local-statistics-of.before:
- **One pair of effects suffices.** Clause (b) exhibits a single pair of
  local rank-one effects that detects the correlation; the two-outcome
  measurements with effects $(P,I-P)$ and $(P',I-P')$ have joint law
  $(s_{2}^{2},s_{1}^{2}-s_{2}^{2},s_{1}^{2}-s_{2}^{2},s_{1}^{2}+s_{2}^{2}-1)$
  in the ordering $(+,+),(+,-),(-,+),(-,-)$ after normalization by
  $\|\Psi\|=1$, whose first entry differs from $s_{1}^{2}s_{2}^{2}$.
pthm-nrqm-composites-local-statistics-of.after:
- **One pair of effects suffices.** Clause (b) exhibits a single pair of
  local rank-one effects that detects the correlation; the two-outcome
  measurements with effects $(P,I-P)$ and $(P',I-P')$ have joint law
  $(0,s_{1}^{2},s_{2}^{2},1-s_{1}^{2}-s_{2}^{2})$
  in the ordering $(+,+),(+,-),(-,+),(-,-)$ for the unit vector $\Psi$.
  All entries are nonnegative because $\sum_{r}s_{r}^{2}=1$, and the first
  entry differs from $s_{1}^{2}s_{2}^{2}$.

lem-nrqm-composites-local-pvm-tensor-ext.before: 1.1 [Strong continuity of tensoring with the identity] Let $M:=\sup_{n}\|S_{n}\|<+\infty$ and let $z\in H\widehat\otimes K$, $\varepsilon>0$. By density [F1] there is a finite sum $z_{0}=\kappa\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^{m}u_{i}\otimes v_{i}\bigr)$ with $\|z-z_{0}\|<\varepsilon/(2M+1)$. Then $\|(S_{n}\otimes I)-(S\otimes I)\|\le M+\|S\|$, and for every $n$ the estimates $\|((S_{n}\otimes I)-(S\otimes I))(z-z_{0})\|\le(M+\|S\|)\|z-z_{0}\|<\varepsilon/2$ and $\|((S_{n}\otimes I)-(S\otimes I))z_{0}\|\le\sum_{i=1}^{m}\|(S_{n}-S)u_{i}\|\,\|v_{i}\|\to0$ hold by [F1]; hence $\|((S_{n}\otimes I)-(S\otimes I))z\|<\varepsilon$ for all large $n$, which is (c). [F1, algebra, choose]
lem-nrqm-composites-local-pvm-tensor-ext.after: 1.1 [Strong continuity of tensoring with the identity] Let $M:=\sup_{n}\|S_{n}\|<+\infty$. Strong convergence gives $\|Sx\|=\lim_{n}\|S_{n}x\|\le M\|x\|$ for every $x\in H$, so $\|S\|\le M$. For $z\in H\widehat\otimes K$ and $\varepsilon>0$, density [F1] gives a finite sum $z_{0}=\kappa\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^{m}u_{i}\otimes v_{i}\bigr)$ with $\|z-z_{0}\|<\varepsilon/(4M+1)$. By linearity and the norm estimate [F1], $\|(S_{n}\otimes I)-(S\otimes I)\|\le M+\|S\|\le2M$, and hence $\|((S_{n}\otimes I)-(S\otimes I))(z-z_{0})\|<\varepsilon/2$ for every $n$ (also when $M=0$, when the left side is zero). On the finite sum, [F1] gives $\|((S_{n}\otimes I)-(S\otimes I))z_{0}\|\le\sum_{i=1}^{m}\|(S_{n}-S)u_{i}\|\,\|v_{i}\|\to0$. This is less than $\varepsilon/2$ for all large $n$, and the triangle inequality proves (c). [F1, algebra, choose]
